text.title: django-decision-tree Procedure
text.summary: Eight steps walking the decision tree at bootstrap or refactor checkpoint, ending with the placement policy the layering choice implies.

step.name: collect-signals
step.action: Fill signals object: team_size, model_count, traffic_req_s, needs_admin, needs_async, bounded_contexts.

step.name: pick-framework
step.action: Apply rule r1-pick-framework using the 5-signal score.

step.name: pick-layering
step.decision-gate: Reject mismatched tiers (clean-arch for < 10 models; simple for ≥ 50).

step.name: audit-deps
step.action: For each: collect 8 signals, set verdict ∈ {adopt, trial, hold, sunset}.

step.name: publish-placement-policy
step.action: Write the per-layer placement policy the chosen tier implies into the onboarding doc: what belongs in views / services / utils / models / serializers / tasks / integrations, and the one-way dependency direction. Rules r7-r12 are the policy text; the decision tree's placement branch is how a developer applies it to one unit of code.
step.output: Placement section of the architecture record / onboarding doc.
step.decision-gate: layering="simple" still requires the direction rule r10; skipping it is what turns a fat-model MVP into a circular-import knot.
